$comment: Machine-enforceable rules learned for Channelplay after the profile was created.
brandlib.load_brand() merges this file into brand['learnedRules']; validate_deck.py reads
learnedRules.rules and enforces every entry. Tier 2 of the three-tier learn protocol — every
rule here must also have a dated entry in LEARNED.md explaining who asked for it and why.
RULE OBJECT
id        required. Prefix with 'LOCAL.' so learned rules are distinguishable from built-in
ones in validator output. Becomes the violation id verbatim. Defaults to
'LEARNED.RULE' when missing, which makes the report useless — always set it.
kind      required. One of the seven kinds below. An unknown kind is reported as an info
violation rather than silently ignored.
value     required. A single value, or a list of values that are all checked.
scope     'any' (default), 'title', 'body' or 'eyebrow'. 'body' means every text shape that
is neither a title nor an eyebrow.
formats   optional. Which artifacts the rule applies to. Omit it and the rule applies
everywhere -- the default, and what every rule written before this field
existed does. Values: 'deck' or 'video' (the artifact kind), or a delivery
format from brand.video.formats: 'landscape', 'square', 'vertical'. A reel is
'vertical'. A misspelled value is REPORTED as an info violation and the rule
stays active everywhere -- a typo must never silently disable a rule.
severity  'error' or 'warn'. 'info' is accepted but reserved for the validator's own
diagnostics. Use 'error' only for something that must block a build; an error is
a hard stop for every future deck in this brand, not a strong opinion.
rule      required in practice. The one-line statement shown in the report.
fix       required in practice. What the author should do instead. Be specific: name the
replacement token, size or wording.
added     ISO date the rule was learned.
source    where it came from, e.g. 'user correction, session 2026-07-30'.
KINDS
forbid_text       value is a string or list of strings. Fires when the string appears in
text in scope. Case-insensitive substring match.
require_text      value is a string or list of strings. Fires when the string appears
NOWHERE in scope. Case-insensitive. Reported once against the whole deck.
forbid_color      value is a hex or list of hexes. Fires when the colour is used anywhere in
the deck. NOTE: colour is checked across every fill, line and text run in
the file — 'scope' is not applied to this kind, so a scoped colour ban is
not currently expressible.
min_font_size     value is a number in points. Fires when a run in scope is smaller.
max_font_size     value is a number in points. Fires when a run in scope is larger.
forbid_font_size  value is a number or list of numbers in points. Fires on an exact match.
regex             value is a Python regular expression, or a list of them. Fires when the
pattern MATCHES text in scope — it is a forbid, always, and always
case-insensitive. There is no require-style regex; use require_text.
An uncompilable pattern is reported as an info violation, not a crash.
SAFETY
A rule that raises is caught and reported as an info violation, so one bad rule can never
abort a validation run. But a malformed FILE — invalid JSON — makes load_brand() raise and
takes every downstream skill with it. After editing, re-load the brand to prove it parses:
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts/lib');import brandlib;
b=brandlib.load_brand('channelplay');print(len(b['learnedRules']['rules']))"
The '$examples' array below is documentation. The validator only reads 'rules'; anything under
a key beginning with '$' is ignored. Copy an example into 'rules', do not enable it in place.

$examples.$note: forbid_text — a word the brand has banned outright. This is the kind to reach for after 'never call it that again'. Prefer voice.forbiddenPhrases in brand.json for placeholder strings that ship with a template; use a local rule for a client-specific or brand-specific ban that came out of a session.
$examples.rule: Channelplay copy is operational, not salesy. These three phrases are not.
$examples.fix: Say what the team actually does: 'one field force covers both brands', not 'synergy'.

$examples.$note: require_text — something that must appear somewhere in the deck. Reported once, against the deck rather than a slide, because absence has no location. Use sparingly: it fires on every deck for this brand forever, including the two-slide ones.
$examples.rule: Client decks carry a confidentiality marker.
$examples.fix: Set meta.confidentiality in the Deck IR so it renders in the footer band.

$examples.$note: forbid_color — the mint-text correction, and the canonical example of a tier 2 rule. Note the scope is written as 'title' for documentation, but this kind checks the whole file: every fill, line and text colour. Do not read a narrow scope here as a narrow check.
$examples.rule: Mint and teal are decorative only; 1.6:1 and 2.7:1 on white. Neither carries text.
$examples.fix: Use mint.700 #1B7A74 for mint-family text, or navy #0F0A6C.
$examples.source: example only — already covered by colorRules.forbiddenText

$examples.$note: min_font_size — a floor tighter than the profile's own type.minBodyPt, for one scope. The profile floor is 10.5pt everywhere; this would raise it for body copy only.
$examples.rule: Body copy on a projected deck does not survive below 11pt.
$examples.fix: Cut the copy. Shrinking type past the floor is how a slide becomes unreadable at the back of a room.

$examples.$note: max_font_size — a ceiling. Useful when a client finds the 54pt cover shouty and the fix is a scale change rather than a per-deck override.
$examples.rule: Slide titles stay at or below 40pt for this client.
$examples.fix: Lower type.deckScalePt.title.size in brand.json rather than fighting it per deck.

$examples.$note: forbid_font_size — bans exact sizes rather than a range. The use for it is catching an off-scale size that keeps reappearing, e.g. a 13pt that belongs to no role in the type scale.
$examples.rule: 13, 15 and 17pt are not steps of the Channelplay type scale.
$examples.fix: Pick the nearest role in type.deckScalePt: 12 body, 14 cardTitle, 18 subtitle.

$examples.$note: regex — for patterns a literal string cannot express. Always a forbid, always case-insensitive. This one catches the trailing-full-stop-on-a-title habit and any digit-space-percent spacing error. Test the pattern before committing it: an uncompilable pattern is reported as info and the rule then checks nothing at all.
$examples.rule: Titles do not end in a full stop, and a percentage sign is closed up to its number.
$examples.fix: Drop the full stop. Write '82%', not '82 %'.

rules.rule: 'solutions' is not used in this brand's copy.
rules.fix: Rewrite the line without 'solutions' -- say what the team actually does.

rules.rule: A headline runs to seven words at most. Eight is where a reel's opening stops landing in the first two seconds.
rules.fix: Cut it to seven words or fewer. Drop the qualifier before the claim, not the claim.
